name: the sessions of a node that is gone are adopted
comments: A persistent subscriber of node4 (server-host) is away when node4 goes. While node4 is down, a
message is published for it on node1 (client-host); then the subscriber comes back to node2. The
message must be there: the cluster adopted node4's session as soon as node4's lease ran out, and
kept collecting for it - not only when its client came back. On the default test cluster of test_cluster.sh,
run from client-host. The grep is the check: xmq_sub -v prints each message it receives with its
cluster: node1@client-host node2@client-host node3@server-host node4@server-host node5@farm-host node6@farm-host

timeline.command: xmq_sub -h server-host -p 2887 -u user -P User-Secret1 -V 5 -c -x 3600 -q 1 -i cluster-orphan -t cluster/test/orphan -W 2 --quiet
xmq_pub -h client-host -p 2884 -u user -P User-Secret1 -V 5 -q 1 -i cluster-orphan-publisher -t cluster/test/orphan -m published-while-away --quiet
xmq_sub -h client-host -p 2885 -u user -P User-Secret1 -V 5 -c -x 3600 -q 1 -i cluster-orphan -t cluster/test/orphan -C 1 -W 10 -v | grep -q '\[published-while-away\]'
